data.question: Should we adopt rule change 2 (block_k 3 → 2) even though companies B and C voted against it, adopt the constitutional change R1 (raising invariants.min_company_on_time_rate from 0.6 to 0.65), or keep the current rules (v1)?
data.background: Proposal 2 passed check and the constitution and improved the main goal on_time_deliveries by +9.2 on 5/5 seeds, but B and C voted it down. Overriding or accepting their objection is an agreement question between the parties, so I should not settle it myself. R1 changes a value in the constitution, and regulation changes must always be decided by a human, even though the current rules already meet the new condition.

options.summary: Lowers the blocking_guard threshold block_k from 3 to 2. Measured: on-time 131.0 (current 121.8, +9.2, improved on 5/5 seeds), late 1.2 (current 10.4), blocked s 985 (current 2404), lowest on-time rate 0.98 (current 0.84), unfinished 0.0, KPI conditions met. However, road violations rise to 34.0 (current 25.8). Utility A / B / C is 45.4 / 37.2 / 19.0 (current 38.4 / 38.9 / 28.8). Votes: A for, B and C against, so adopting it means overriding a majority of the companies.
options.stakeholders: Customers of all companies gain the most: far fewer late deliveries, and the worst company's on-time rate rises from 0.84 to 0.98. Company A gains (utility 38.4 → 45.4). Company B loses slightly (38.9 → 37.2). Company C loses heavily (28.8 → 19.0, about a third of its utility). Other road users may be affected by the rise in road violations (25.8 → 34.0).

options.summary: Raises the constitutional floor invariants.min_company_on_time_rate from 0.60 to 0.65. It passed the constitution check, and the current rules already meet it (current lowest on-time rate 0.84), so today's operation does not change. Future rule proposals that would push any company's on-time rate below 0.65 would be rejected automatically. It stays below the KPI condition of 0.7.
options.stakeholders: Customers of the worst-served company gain a firmer guaranteed minimum. Companies lose some freedom for future rule changes that trade one company's on-time rate for overall throughput. There is no immediate change in utility for A, B or C.

options.summary: Stays at v1. On-time 121.8, late 10.4, blocked s 2404, road violations 25.8, lowest on-time rate 0.84, unfinished 0.0. Utility A / B / C is 38.4 / 38.9 / 28.8. The KPI condition (≥ 0.7) is met.
options.stakeholders: B and C keep their current utility and their objection to 2 is respected. Customers forgo about 9.2 additional on-time deliveries and keep about 10.4 late deliveries per run. A forgoes the gain it would get from 2.

recommendation.reason: R1 is low-risk. The current rules already satisfy it, it does not change today's operation, and it moves the constitutional floor toward the human's provisional KPI floor of 0.7, which fits the goal that no company's customers wait badly. Proposal 2 is strongly better for customers and for the KPI on every measured seed. Still, it overrides two of three companies, cuts C's utility by about a third, and increases road violations, and I cannot explain why. I suggest asking B and C for their reasons, and checking what the extra road violations mean, before deciding on 2. R1 and 2 are not mutually exclusive, so the human may also adopt both.

unknowns: Why C's utility drops from 28.8 to 19.0 under proposal 2 while the lowest on-time rate rises to 0.98: the components of each company's utility function are not shown.
Per-company on-time rates and delivery counts under proposal 2 (only the town-wide totals and the minimum are measured).
Whether the rise in road violations (25.8 → 34.0) is a safety concern or a minor rule infraction, and who bears it.
How B and C would change their behavior (or cooperation) if their votes were overridden.
How customers perceive the change in late deliveries, and whether they notice the difference.
Next period's demand level and mix; results are from 5 seeds under the current demand only.
Whether a future rule change would be blocked by R1's 0.65 floor, and whether the human intends to raise the constitutional floor further toward 0.7.
